config.classes_note: Two classes, sourced from the field by locus: WikiWho as an authorship-attribution service for revisioned (wiki) content (B2 infobox and lede; B1 and B3, the WWW 2014 title), which is the census's lineage 'authorship and reuse' as the field states it; and WikiWho as token-level provenance of text (B1 Introduction; B3 nutshell; B2 Technical details), which is the census's provenance object. The census's kind, 'algorithm and API', is stated by the field (B1 'WikiWho Algorithm', 'The WikiWho API') but names no class the archive could apply a category to, and is not run. No field source places WikiWho in a class of the archive's own: 'provenance meta-aggregator' is the census's class, an archive source, ledgered as PE claims and not run as an O-class, since the brief confines classes to what B sources. The aliases are the entity's name, its two hosts (wikiwho.wmcloud.org, the census's url; wikiwho.net, the GESIS host the README names), its service WhoColor, the tool it powers (Who Wrote That?) and its first author, Fabian Flöck (B1 Contributors). 'wikiHow' is a homonym of the near-name kind and is not an alias: the pattern \bwikiwho\b does not match 'wikihow'. Admission by reading (§3.4): a candidate is admitted when its sentence or paragraph makes a claim bearing on WikiWho, or applies an archive category to authorship attribution of revisioned content, or to token-level provenance of text, as a class; a bare mention, a sentence on authorship attribution of a literary corpus (the archive's heteronym and Plato-Aristotle work, whose object is not revisioned wiki content), or a sentence on provenance in general is not a claim on the entity or its classes.
